title: Anthropic's Workflow Patterns: Simple Over Complex

questions.question: How does Anthropic distinguish a workflow from an agent?
options: Workflows are engineer-owned predefined graphs; agents are model-owned dynamic tool direction
Workflows always use embeddings for retrieval, while agents always call tools directly without any retrieval step
Workflows run only on CPU instances; agents require dedicated GPU inference hardware
Workflows are always stateless between calls; agents automatically persist state across every call
questions.explanation: Workflow = predefined code path the engineer owns; agent = the model owns the graph.

questions.question: What are the three capabilities of the augmented LLM that underpins all five patterns?
options: Embeddings, fine-tuning, and retrieval-augmented generation pipelines
Search (retrieval), tools (actions), memory (persistence)
Vector, KV, and graph stores, wired together behind one retrieval interface
Plan, execute, and reflect, cycling through a fixed three-step loop each turn
questions.explanation: The atomic unit is one LLM with retrieval, tools, and memory wired in.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the five Anthropic workflow patterns?
options: Prompt chaining, where output of one call feeds the next
Routing, where a classifier LLM picks the downstream handler
Gradient distillation, a model-compression training technique
Evaluator-optimizer, where one LLM iteratively critiques another's draft
questions.explanation: The five are prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer. Gradient distillation is a training concept.

questions.question: Which two shapes does parallelization come in?
options: Sync and async calls, chosen based on whether the caller can block
Hot and cold paths, split by how frequently each branch executes
Sectioning (different chunks) and voting (same prompt N times, aggregate)
Stateful and stateless workers, split by whether they persist between calls
questions.explanation: Parallelization is sectioning or voting; both fan out N calls and aggregate.

questions.question: Which workflow pattern is Self-Refine generalized?
options: Evaluator-optimizer, where one LLM proposes and another critiques
Prompt chaining, where each call's output feeds directly into the next
Routing, where a classifier decides which downstream handler runs
Orchestrator-workers, where one LLM dynamically assigns work to others
questions.explanation: Evaluator-optimizer is the Anthropic name for the Self-Refine / CRITIC iterative pattern.

questions.question: When do workflows beat agents according to the lesson?
options: Always, since workflows strictly dominate agents in every situation, regardless of how unpredictable the task is
On predictable, cost-bounded, or compliance-bounded tasks where the graph can be enumerated and audited
Only for simple, single-turn chat interfaces with no tool use
Only when the deployment runs entirely on dedicated GPU hardware
questions.explanation: Workflows are cheaper, easier to debug, and auditable; pick them when steps are knowable.
